english.title: Possess component parts of ammunition with intent to manufacture
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) possessed

(A)_[component parts]_
(B)_[a component part]_

of ammunition, namely

(C)_[a bullet,]_
(D)_[bullets,]_
(E)_[a cartridge case,]_
(F)_[cartridge cases,]_
(G)_[a primer,]_
(H)_[primers,]_
(I)_[a propellant,]_
(J)_[propellants,]_
(K)_[**(..SPECIFY COMBINATION OF ABOVE..),]_

intending to manufacture ammunition to which section 1 of the Firearms Act 1968 applied, using

(L)_[that part]_
(M)_[those parts]_

when, were you to do so,

(N)_[possession of the ammunition by you would constitute an offence under section 1]_
(O)_[the manufacture or possession of the ammunition by you would constitute an offence under section 3]_

of the Act
english.legislation: Contrary to section 3A of the Firearms Act 1968.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6 / 12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 5 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction depends on the general limit in a magistrates’ court and may be 6 or 12 months depending on the date of conviction, see section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
